newsitem.title: CONGO: Zaire peace talks start, South Africa says.
newsitem.headline: Zaire peace talks start, South Africa says.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila began their first direct talks on Sunday with South Africa's Nelson Mandela acting as host, Mandela's spokesman said.
"The discussions have reached a critical point," spokesman Parks Mankahlana told reporters on board the South African naval ship SAS Outeniqua, which was in Congo's port of Pointe Noire.
The three men had been meeting for more than one hour, Mankahlana said just before 1 p.m. (1200 GMT).

Before the talks began, a South African official said that Mobutu had agreed in principle to stand down and clear the way for a transitional process. Kabila told Reuters from the ship that Mobutu should quit immediately.
The talks, initially planned for Friday, had been due to take place in international waters. "The question of going into international waters has not been raised yet," Mandela's spokesman said.
